extraction.pages_processed: 1-61 (all pages keyword-screened; the step assessments containing hits read in full: pages 11-22 (permits, e-government, state aid, customs, cybersecurity), 25-27 (public investment), 34-35 (labour inspectorate), 38, 43, 46, 48, 50 and 55-60)
extraction.notes: RUN-2026-02 stage 7 extraction (rules 0.5). Keyword screen of the whole text: digital, cyber, artificial intelligence, AI, e-government, e-services, electronic, data protection, personal data, interoperability, broadband, 5G, gigabit, connectivity, eID, identification, signature, trust service, online, ICT, IT, information society, roaming, internet, MConnect, MPass, MSign, MCloud, EVO, workers, EURES, social security, foreign, free movement, freedom of movement, labour, Chapter 2, EHIC, health insurance card, migration, diaspora. The source-quality finding of passing mentions is not confirmed for this annex: three Reform Agenda steps assessed here are in scope, the e-government ecosystem step (pages 14-15), the Customs Decision System step (pages 17-19, flagged theme_doubtful as in MDA-EU-2025-002) and the cybersecurity agency and CERT step (pages 19-23), and one online service sits inside the beneficial ownership step (page 58). For each in-scope step the Commission's results, the beneficiary's view and the Commission's conclusion are extracted; the step, description and baseline cells restate the Reform Agenda steps already held in MDA-EU-2025-002 and are not extracted again; the lists of evidence documents (checks performed) are not extracted. Not extracted: accession to the Common Transit Convention (page 17, customs procedure with no digital claim); the digitalised exchange of tax and customs information (page 6) and the public investment IT platforms and their interoperability (pages 25-27), tax, customs and back-office systems out by default; the labour inspectorate step (page 35), general labour-market policy outside the Chapter 2 boundary; the energy market IT platforms, the Green Home platform, the guarantees of origin register and the register of seized criminal assets (pages 43, 46, 50, 55-56, 59-60), sector systems; budget documents published online (page 7, incidental); media legislation and foreign interference (page 2).
